title: Obama Presidential Library: White House Office of Presidential Correspondence and Office of Public Engagement Records Concerning Jens Söring (2009–2017)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This is a request under the Presidential Records Act, 44 U.S.C. §§ 2201–2209, and the Freedom of Information Request 

Time frame of the request: January 20, 2009 to January 20, 2017. 

1. Records requested

Records created or received by the White House Office of Presidential Correspondence and the White House Office of Public Engagement (including its Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs predecessor or successor offices) concerning Jens Söring, a German national then held in a Virginia prison. This request is separate from my earlier request on White House Counsel and inter-agency records and does not seek the same records.

a. Logs and tracking data: database entries, tally sheets, or correspondence logs tracking mail, petitions, e-mails, or postcards referencing Söring.
b. Mail analysis: periodic mail analysis reports, correspondence summaries, or sample mail packets prepared for senior staff that mention Söring or related letter campaigns.
c. Response templates and clearances: draft and final form letters, talking points, and clearance or routing sheets (including clearances with the NSC, the Department of State, or the Department of Justice) for responding to inquiries about Söring.
d. Referral records: routing slips, referral logs, or transmittals sending Söring-related correspondence to other White House offices or agencies for reply.
e. Petitions and appeals: correspondence, petitions, or formal appeals regarding Söring from the German Embassy, members of the German Bundestag, German government officials, advocacy organizations, or public figures. Author John Grisham was vocal in his support. Please search for correspondence from Grisham. 
f. Representative sample: where mail campaigns generated large volumes of near-identical correspondence, I ask for a representative sample, and I do not require every individual item.



2. Where to search

• Office of Presidential Correspondence files (correspondence management, presidential letters and messages, mail analysis)

• Office of Public Engagement files

• WHORM subject and name file indices and tracking records for incoming correspondence on this topic

3. Search terms

Primary: "Jens Söring" OR "Jens Soering" OR "Jens Sorin" OR "Söring" OR "Soering" OR "Elizabeth Haysom" OR "Haysom"

Contextual: "Bundestag" OR "German Embassy" OR "Auswärtiges Amt" OR "Transfer of Sentenced Persons" OR "Council of Europe" OR "prisoner transfer" OR "repatriation" OR "clemency" OR "pardon" OR "Virginia" OR "petition"

4. Segregability, classification, and withholdings

Please release all reasonably segregable portions of any record withheld in part, and identify the specific PRA or FOIA exemption on the face of each redaction. For any withheld document, please provide an itemized description (date, author, recipient, type, exemption). I will accept redaction of the names and contact information of private citizens under (b)(6), but ask that organizations, officials, and public figures be left unredacted. If any responsive record is classified, I request mandatory declassification review under E.O. 13526 §3.5.om of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, for records of the Obama administration. 

Thank you for the work that the Obama Presidential library does each and every day, and thank you for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
